article_content: Mia Tui founder Charlotte Jamme faces legal challenges from TUI AG over trademark rights. The London-based handbag company, which still manufactures in Vietnam and employs two full-time staff, received opposition to its name trademark application from the German conglomerate (parent company of Thomson and First Choice). While Mia Tui operates under Class 18 trademarks for leather goods and TUI AG specializes in travel services, the corporation claims potential consumer confusion regarding their similarly branded products, including rucksacks. Jamme, who established her brand in 2010 with a logo trademark and relocated to the UK in 2011, maintains: 'You're either buying a holiday or a bag.' The dispute now awaits resolution by the UK Intellectual Property Office, with TUI AG stating it must protect its brand against dilution.

Nonostante Mia Tui operi nel settore pelletteria (marchio Classe 18) e TUI AG in quello turistico, la corporation sostiene il rischio di confusione per prodotti come gli zaini. Jamme, che registrò il logo nel 2010 e trasferì la sede nel Regno Unito nel 2011, ribatte: 'Si compra una vacanza o una borsa, non ci sono ambiguità.' La controversia, ora all'attenzione dell'Ufficio Brevetti britannico, vede TUI AG determinata a proteggere la propria identità di marca.

article_content: As Cesc Fabregas prepares to face Arsenal with Chelsea this weekend, Sportsmail's Phil Duncan examines key questions surrounding the midfielder. Will he receive boos? Would he celebrate a goal? Was Arsene Wenger justified in retaining Mesut Ozil rather than re-signing him? Fabregas, who developed into a world-class talent at Arsenal before becoming club captain, now returns to Stamford Bridge in Chelsea colors. While some supporters find this transition uncomfortable, the situation stems from Arsenal's decision not to reacquire him, leaving Chelsea as his sole London option for pursuing silverware. Unlike Emmanuel Adebayor's notorious celebration against Arsenal in 2009, Fabregas is anticipated to demonstrate restraint if he scores, maintaining deference to his developmental club. His standout Arsenal moments include dominating Juventus' midfield in 2006's Champions League, a gutsy penalty conversion against Barcelona in 2010 while injured, and a memorable solo effort against Tottenham. While Fabregas' solitary 2005 FA Cup triumph with Arsenal underscores the team's diminished competitiveness in the post-Patrick Vieira era, Wenger's choice to persist with Ozil appears strategic given the German's overlapping playmaking role and Aaron Ramsey's ascendance. Nevertheless, Fabregas' instant Premier League impact with Chelsea confirms his enduring quality.

article_content: NEW YORK: The dollar dropped to a six-week low on Friday as economic data revealed weaker-than-expected job growth, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain current interest rates in December. The dollar index fell 1.1% to 105.03, marking its largest single-day decline since July. October's nonfarm payrolls showed 150,000 new jobs, below the anticipated 180,000. September's figures were revised downward to 297,000 from 336,000. Lazard's chief market strategist Ronald Temple described the numbers as a 'Goldilocks' scenario - sufficient for economic needs without fueling inflation. The yen strengthened to 149.18 per dollar, while the euro rose 1.1% to $1.0735. Sterling reached a six-week high of $1.2389, posting its best daily gain since January. U.S. 10-year Treasury yields fell to 4.484%, the lowest in five weeks, following supply adjustments and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's moderated policy stance. Market pricing now suggests less than 5% chance of December rate hike, down from 20% earlier in the week, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

article_content: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors passed an 8-3 majority vote Tuesday banning toy inclusions in children's fast-food meals lacking updated nutritional compliance. The veto-proof legislation proceeds to Mayor Gavin Newsom's desk, though his potential rejection would be overridden given the supermajority support. McDonald's spokesperson Danya Proud contested the decision: 'This contradicts customer preferences. We've introduced healthier choices including apple slices and low-fat milk while committing to further improvements.' Supervisor Eric Mar, citing his fifth-grade daughter's demographic group with quadrupled obesity rates since 1980, championed the measure. Supporting data from Yale's Rudd Center revealed only 12 of 3,000 kids' meal combinations met preschool nutrition standards, contrasted against $4.2B annual fast-food advertising expenditures. Mandated changes effective December 2011 require meals under 600 calories with <35% fat content. Each serving must contain ½ cup fruit, ¾ cup vegetables, and stay below 640mg sodium. Breakfast options allow fruit/vegetable substitutions. City officials expect legal challenges from restaurant chains, though McDonald's hasn't disclosed specific legal strategies.

La legge, immune a potenziali veti grazie alla maggioranza qualificata, affronta il preoccupante aumento dei casi di obesità infantile correlato a tre decenni di commercializzazione degli Happy Meal. Danya Proud, portavoce di McDonald's, ha espresso forte contrarietà: 'Non rispecchia le richieste dei clienti. Abbiamo ampliato le scelte salutari con mele già sbucciate e latte a basso contenuto lipidico.' article_content: Ryan Giggs maintains Manchester United's commitment to youth development remains strong despite recent changes. The sale of academy graduate Danny Welbeck to Arsenal and substantial summer transfer spending had raised questions about shifting priorities at Old Trafford. United boast a historic record of fielding at least one homegrown player in every matchday squad since 1937 - a streak potentially challenged by Welbeck's departure. Giggs, now assistant manager under Louis van Gaal, stated: 'The club's philosophy remains unchanged. Our tradition combines exciting football with youth opportunities. While Danny's exit is disappointing, Van Gaal has consistently developed young talent - from Seedorf and Kluivert at Ajax to current players like Tyler Blackett, who's featured in every game this season. Below Rooney and Van Persie in the pecking order, we have Januzaj and Wilson progressing.' United invested over £150m in summer 2014 signings following last season's seventh-place finish, including record signing Ángel Di María and Radamel Falcao on loan. Nicky Butt, coaching United's U21s, acknowledged evolving priorities: 'Clubs must adapt. While maintaining youth pathways, our immediate focus is restoring competitiveness. Danny's move balanced his England aspirations with club needs during this transitional phase.'

article_content: The prime suspect in the 2004 murder of 21-year-old Juilliard student Sarah Fox maintains his innocence while claiming supernatural communication with the victim. Dimitry Sheinman told the New York Post that Fox 'speaks' to him from beyond the grave, asserting her desire for the 'real killer' to be found. Fox's body was discovered six days after her disappearance in Inwood Hill Park, positioned with two dozen yellow tulip petals nearby. Sheinman became the primary suspect after sharing unreleased case details during police interviews, though no physical evidence connected him to the crime. Now residing in Cape Town with his family since 2006, Sheinman works as a self-described psychic healer. Investigators reportedly told The Post they still consider him the likely perpetrator, stating: 'There's no real doubt it's him, but we haven't proved it yet.' Sheinman claims to have identified another suspect through visions in 2012, but police dismissed this individual after previous clearance. The suspect's wife described the ongoing trauma for their two daughters, hoping for 'normal lives' in South Africa.

article_content: A South African chef residing in New Zealand since 2007 claims his work visa renewal was denied due to health concerns. Immigration New Zealand stated the decision resulted from multiple obesity-related medical conditions and projected healthcare costs, not weight alone. Albertus Buitenhuis, 50, reduced his weight from 160kg to 126kg but faces chronic knee issues, impaired glucose tolerance, and fatty liver disease. The agency estimated $16,000 for potential knee surgery and noted risks of diabetes and cardiovascular complications. While Buitenhuis acknowledges nations' right to screen immigrants, he contends officials delayed health warnings until his residency application. The couple, now without legal status, faces financial strain awaiting appeal. Experts highlight this case reflects global debates about balancing public health costs with immigration equity.

article_content: A 73-year-old Maryland resident died Monday after being struck twice by an unoccupied vehicle that rolled downhill in Edgewater. Lee Sheila Mahoney was walking near her home when a 2010 Ford Mustang - left without its parking brake engaged - began descending the gently sloped street. The vehicle initially struck Mahoney and came to rest atop her, according to Anne Arundel County Police. Vehicle owner David Adam Garman, 23, witnessed the movement and attempted retrieval. Police confirm Garman reversed the car while unaware Mahoney remained trapped beneath. Emergency responders transported Mahoney to Anne Arundel Medical Center, where she was pronounced dead. Records indicate Mahoney and her husband resided in their home for nearly 40 years. Social media tributes emphasized her community role, with one friend stating: 'Lee helped raise almost every kid on this street.' Family members called her 'the heart and soul of our family.' Police spokesperson Justin Mulcahy cited 'driver error' due to improper parking brake use and failure to turn wheels toward the curb. The investigation continues with the State's Attorney's Office, pending potential charges.

article_content: Chris and Gabby Adcock secured Commonwealth Games gold for England with a decisive 21-9 21-12 victory over teammates Chris Langridge and Heather Olver in the mixed doubles final. The top-seeded couple dominated the 35-minute match at Glasgow's Emirates Arena, maintaining their tournament-long record of not conceding a single game. The Adcocks' flawless performance saw them never concede more than 17 points per game across five matches. Gabby Adcock added this gold to her women's doubles bronze and team silver medals. While Langridge and Olver were outplayed in the final, both contributed to England's team silver, with Langridge also earning men's doubles bronze. Badminton England may reconsider the Langridge/Olver partnership before the 2016 Olympics. The Adcocks, married since 2013, have strengthened their Rio Olympic prospects through this non-ranking event victory, building on their partnership revival after Chris's 2012 Olympic pairing with Scotland's Imogen Bankier. Gabby Adcock stated: "We maintained composure under pressure as top seeds. Though exhausted, we're thrilled with this achievement." The players now plan to reunite with their dog Bowser in Milton Keynes, with Chris calling their final performance "a perfect game on this special stage."

article_content: The U.S.-China technology rivalry escalated this week with updated AI chip export regulations from the Biden administration. These measures could significantly impact Chinese tech giants' ability to advance in artificial intelligence development. The U.S. Commerce Department expanded its October 2022 export controls on Tuesday, aiming to address technological advancements and prevent loophole exploitation. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo stated the updates aim to restrict China's access to advanced chips critical for military and AI applications, as reported by the Financial Times. This policy shift comes ahead of a potential Biden-Xi summit, further complicating bilateral relations. Major AI chip manufacturers Nvidia, AMD, and Intel face immediate challenges. Their high-performance chips, essential for training advanced AI models, now face export limitations. Nvidia must halt shipments of two China-specific processors (H800 and A800 GPUs) developed to comply with previous restrictions. Intel's Gaudi2 chip also falls under the new controls. Nvidia's shares fell 6% following the announcement, with 25% of its data center chip revenue coming from China. Chinese firms may now rely on older chips like Nvidia's 2017 V100 model for AI training, potentially increasing costs and development timelines compared to U.S. counterparts. Despite $5 billion in pending orders from Chinese tech leaders like Alibaba and Tencent, delivery uncertainties persist. While stockpiling and unofficial channels may provide temporary relief, analysts predict long-term competitive disadvantages for China's AI sector. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged challenges but expressed confidence in global demand offsetting Chinese market impacts. Concurrently, U.S. tech giants Microsoft and Google are developing proprietary AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia, while Intel expands its foundry services.

Queens Park Rangers defender Rio Ferdinand received a £25,000 fine and three-match ban for using the derogatory term 'sket' in a September tweet. Since the 2010-11 season, the FA has investigated 121 social media misconduct cases, with 60 resulting in charges. Ferdinand must complete an educational program within four months as part of his penalty. Notable cases include Benoit Assou-Ekotto's £50,000 fine for supporting Nicolas Anelka's controversial 'quenelle' gesture, Ashley Cole's £90,000 penalty for describing the FA as a 'bunch of t****ts', and Ryan Babel's £10,000 fine for posting an altered image of referee Howard Webb. All fine revenues are reinvested into football development programs.

article_content: I typically catch myself before using the 'p-word' (perfection) with my daughters, though occasionally it slips out - like when complimenting their holiday outfits. As someone who's battled lifelong perfectionism, I immediately regret these moments, fearing I'll pass on this burdensome trait. This pattern began with striving to be the ideal daughter and student, later extending to career, marriage, and motherhood. Progress for me now means prioritizing sleep over waking at 4:30 AM to craft polished writing. Debora Spar, Barnard College president and author of 'Wonder Women: Sex, Power and the Quest for Perfection', examines how modern women transformed feminist opportunities into oppressive perfectionism. Nearly 50 years after Betty Friedan's 'The Feminine Mystique', Spar argues we've created unrealistic expectations of effortless success across all life domains. Spar cites 1970s advertising like Revlon's Charlie perfume campaign - featuring model Shelley Hack as a flawless working mother - as fueling this myth. 'We expected to glide through complex lives without struggle or failure,' Spar notes, 'then feel inadequate when reality proves messy.' The book offers five strategies: 1) Transparent dialogue about life's tradeoffs 2) Strategic refusal of non-essential tasks 3) Guilt-free prioritization 4) 'Satisficing' (accepting good-enough outcomes) from economic theory 5) Engaging men as equal partners in domestic responsibilities.

Questo meccanismo è partito dal voler essere la figlia e studentessa modello, per poi estendersi alla carriera, matrimonio e maternità. Oggi il mio progresso si misura nel privilegiare il sonno invece di svegliarmi alle 4:30 per scrivere testi perfetti. A 50 anni da 'La mistica della femminilità' di Betty Friedan, Spar sostiene che ci siamo create aspettative irrealistiche di successo senza intoppi in ogni ambito vitale. Spar cita esempi pubblicitari anni '70 come la campagna del profumo Charlie di Revlon, con la modella Shelley Hack nel ruolo di madre-lavoratrice impeccabile, come alimentatori di questo mito. 'Credevamo di poter scivolare attraverso esistenze complesse senza intoppi o fallimenti,' osserva Spar, 'per poi sentirci inadeguate quando la realtà si rivela disordinata.' Il libro propone cinque strategie: 1) Onestà sui compromessi della vita 2) Rifiuto strategico di impegni superflui 3) Priorità senza sensi di colpa 4) 'Soddisfare' (accettare risultati sufficienti) dalla teoria economica 5) Coinvolgere gli uomini come partner paritari nella gestione domestica.

article_content: Justin Lookadoo, a self-described Christian relationship advisor, has drawn widespread criticism following a controversial presentation at Richardson High School in Dallas, Texas. The former juvenile probation officer, known for his 'Dateable' program, allegedly told students that women should 'know how to shut up' to attract dates while encouraging men to 'fight battles' and keep women 'covered up.' During Wednesday's event, multiple students walked out of the assembly while others challenged Lookadoo's assertions. One student questioned, 'Why focus on telling girls to leave abusive relationships rather than teaching boys not to abuse?' Social media reactions escalated with the hashtag #lookadouche, where users condemned his remarks as misogynistic. Lookadoo's YouTube content and book – which he describes as a bestseller – emphasize traditional gender roles, stating: 'Dateable girls let men lead – God made guys as leaders.' His advice for boys includes maintaining dominance and avoiding pornography. While Lookadoo defended his approach as 'empowering,' Richardson School District officials acknowledged community concerns and apologized for 'any distress caused' by the event.

article_content: Princess Anne, managing Gloucestershire's Gatcombe Park estate for 40 years, advocates gassing as a humane badger culling alternative to shooting. In a BBC Countryfile interview, she stated: 'Gas allows badgers to essentially fall asleep, unlike firearms.' This follows Environment Secretary Owen Paterson maintaining culls despite a 2023 report deeming Somerset/Gloucestershire 'controlled shooting' ineffective. Anne links bovine TB outbreaks - which reduced her herds by a third since 2021 - to growing badger populations threatening other species. Her pro-GM crop stance conflicts with Prince Charles' environmental concerns, while her horsemeat proposal aims to address equine neglect through commercial value creation. Zoological Society of London's Prof. Rosie Woodroffe countered that 1982's gassing ban resulted from Porton Down experiments showing badgers suffered in poorly ventilated setts. She advocates vaccination programs instead. Humane Society International's Mark Jones condemned reviving 'inhumane' methods causing slow deaths.

In un'intervista a BBC Countryfile ha dichiarato: 'Con il gas i tassi si addormentano, a differenza di quanto avviene con gli spari'. The world No. 144 delivered an electrifying performance marked by 37 aces and 70 winners across four sets, becoming the first player outside the top 100 since Andrei Olhovskiy's 1992 upset to defeat a reigning world No. 1 at a Grand Slam. Despite Nadal's trademark resilience - having rallied from first-set losses in three previous matches - Kyrgios maintained relentless precision. The teenager's unconventional approach stood in stark contrast to his opponent's rituals, with Kyrgios casually waving to fans before unleashing 130mph serves. Pivotal moments included a between-the-legs 'hotdog' winner and a Hawk-Eye challenge that reversed a second-round match point against him. While Nadal briefly claimed the second set, Kyrgios rebounded with what he called his 'juicy wiggle' celebration after securing victory. This upset extends Nadal's Wimbledon struggles, following 2013's first-round exit to Steve Darcis and 2012's loss to Lukas Rosol. Kyrgios now faces Milos Raonic in the quarterfinals, potentially reshaping conversations about tennis' next generation.

article_content: Actress Mia Farrow provided testimony on Monday claiming fashion model Naomi Campbell attributed mysterious diamonds to former Liberian president Charles Taylor. This occurred during Taylor's war crimes trial at the UN-backed Special Court for Sierra Leone, where prosecutors allege he funded violence through conflict diamonds - gems mined in war zones to finance military activities. Farrow's account contradicts Campbell's testimony from last week, where the model expressed uncertainty about stones delivered to her Pretoria hotel room in 1997. 'She described nighttime visitors claiming to represent Taylor, who gave her a large diamond,' Farrow stated under oath. Both women attended a Nelson Mandela-hosted dinner that year alongside Taylor. Campbell confirmed discussing the incident with Farrow and former agent Carole White the next morning. While recalling a comment that 'This must be from Charles Taylor,' she couldn't identify who made the statement. Prosecutors announced plans to call two witnesses offering conflicting accounts. Taylor faces charges including sexual slavery, terrorism, and crimes against humanity tied to Sierra Leone's civil war (1991-2002), marked by child soldier conscription and systematic violence. Though prosecutors closed their case in February 2009, they reopened it in June after learning about the diamond incident. Court filings state this evidence aims to show Taylor's alleged use of conflict diamonds for personal enrichment and arms procurement - claims he denies.

L'accusa sostiene che Taylor abbia finanziato il conflitto attraverso diamanti insanguinati - minerali estratti in zone di guerra per finanziare operazioni militari. La versione della Farrow contraddice la testimonianza resa dalla Campbell la scorsa settimana, dove la modella aveva espresso incertezza sull'origine dei diamanti ricevuti nella sua stanza d'albergo a Pretoria nel 1997. 'Ha descritto visitatori notturni che affermavano di agire per conto di Taylor, consegnandole un grosso diamante,' ha dichiarato la Farrow sotto giuramento. Tutti i partecipanti avevano preso parte a una cena ospitata da Nelson Mandela nello stesso anno. La Campbell ha confermato di aver discusso l'accaduto con la Farrow e l'ex agente Carole White la mattina seguente. Pur ricordando un commento del tipo 'Questo deve venire da Charles Taylor,' non ha potuto identificare chi lo avesse pronunciato. L'accusa ha annunciato di voler chiamare due testimoni con versioni contrastanti dei fatti. Taylor è imputato per crimini che includono schiavitù sessuale, terrorismo e crimini contro l'umanità legati alla guerra civile in Sierra Leone (1991-2002), caratterizzata dal reclutamento di bambini soldato e violenze sistematiche. Nonostante la chiusura iniziale del caso nel febbraio 2009, i pubblici ministeri lo hanno riaperto a giugno dopo aver appreso dell'episodio dei diamanti. Documenti giudiziari sostengono che queste prove dimostrerebbero il presunto utilizzo di diamanti insanguinati da parte di Taylor per arricchimento personale e acquisto di armamenti - accuse che l'ex presidente nega.

article_content: Manchester City has officially opened its revolutionary £200 million Etihad Campus, setting a new benchmark for football training facilities worldwide. This milestone starkly contrasts with the club's modest past, where players trained at dated complexes like Platt Lane and shared space with rivals Manchester United at Carrington - complete with its legendary Scottish security guard Michael. The sprawling new complex features 16 pitches, a 7,000-capacity academy stadium, and educational facilities for local youth. Sportsmail's Martin Keown recently toured the site with club legend Patrick Vieira, witnessing amenities ranging from altitude chambers to culinary training spaces. Old-timers recall vastly different conditions. The Carrington era (shared with Manchester United) saw media briefings in makeshift rooms, Kevin Keegan's head tennis matches delaying press conferences, and Joey Barton using training grounds as a personal driving range. Security consisted of Michael's intimidating booth decorated with team memorabilia - a far cry from today's high-tech surveillance. Managerial tenures brought distinct personalities: Sven-Goran Eriksson's charm won staff loyalty, while Roberto Mancini cycled to work with a support car trailing behind. The facility witnessed infamous player clashes, like Mario Balotelli's training ground brawl with Micah Richards, often visible to public observers. While rivals obsess over privacy, City cultivated community ties - even inviting a pitch-spying fan for an official visit. The new campus' remote location now challenges players commuting from Cheshire's affluent suburbs, proving that even state-of-the-art facilities can't eliminate all complaints.

La posizione periferica del nuovo campus ora complica gli spostamenti dei calciatori dalle ricche aree residenziali del Cheshire, dimostrando che nemmeno strutture all'avanguardia eliminano ogni lamentela.

article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) – A 73-year-old woman in China's Jiangxi province became the first recorded human fatality from H10N8 avian influenza earlier this month. The patient, hospitalized on November 30 with severe pneumonia and multiple pre-existing conditions including hypertension and heart disease, passed away on December 6. World Health Organization reports indicate she visited a live poultry market four days before symptom onset. China's National Health Commission stated: 'Expert analysis suggests this is an isolated case with low human transmission risk.' Health authorities confirmed no infections among her close contacts. Dr. Leo Poon of Hong Kong University noted H10N8 appears less concerning than H7N9, which has caused 45 deaths in China since its 2013 emergence. While H10N8 previously infected two Australian abattoir workers in 2010, those cases were mild. Current public health advisories emphasize hand hygiene and avoiding poultry contact in outbreak regions.

La Commissione Nazionale per la Salute cinese ha dichiarato: 'Le analisi degli esperti indicano un caso isolato con basso rischio di trasmissione umana.' Le autorità sanitarie hanno confermato che nessuno dei suoi contatti stretti è stato contagiato. Il dottor Leo Poon dell'Università di Hong Kong ha evidenziato che l'H10N8 appare meno preoccupante dell'H7N9, responsabile di 45 decessi in Cina dal suo primo rilevamento nel 2013. Le attuali linee guida sanitarie raccomandano rigorosa igiene delle mani ed evitare il contatto con pollame nelle zone interessate.

article_content: After over 50 years of secrecy, the U.S. Department of Energy has declassified documents from the 1950s security clearance hearing of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the Manhattan Project. The newly released transcripts offer insights into atomic bomb development and the anti-communist fervor that shaped post-WWII America. Oppenheimer directed the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos National Laboratory, which produced the atomic weapons used on Hiroshima (August 6, 1945) and Nagasaki (August 9, 1945). Following World War II, he faced a four-week closed-door hearing that revoked his security clearance amid allegations of communist ties involving his family and associates. Steven Aftergood of the Federation of American Scientists noted the documents reveal nuanced details about nuclear weapons development debates and demonstrate Oppenheimer's unjust treatment. 'This case represents a peak of anti-communist anxiety that damaged the reputation of America's preeminent scientist,' he stated. While portions of the transcripts were previously released with redactions, this full disclosure provides scholars with internal discussions about atomic espionage and hydrogen bomb development. Oppenheimer received the Enrico Fermi Award in 1963 as partial rehabilitation, years before his death from throat cancer in 1967.

article_content: The family of VonDerrit Myers Jr., an 18-year-old African-American man fatally shot on October 8, 2023, by an off-duty St. Louis police officer, has identified the shooter as Jason H. Flanery. Authorities had withheld the officer's name pending a threat assessment. Independent autopsy results from Dr. Cyril Wecht show Myers sustained eight gunshot wounds, including six entry wounds in the posterior legs. The fatal projectile entered through his right cheek. The St. Louis Medical Examiner's preliminary report confirmed multiple lower body injuries but did not analyze shot trajectories. Attorney Jermaine Wooten presented alleged social media posts by Flanery containing criticisms of former President Obama, derogatory remarks about Michelle Obama, and negative comments regarding LGBTQ+ individuals. Wooten contends these posts demonstrate racial bias relevant to the case. Police reports state Myers fired first during the encounter, supported by gunshot residue found on his clothing. Flanery's attorney Brian Millikan claims the autopsy supports the officer's account, asserting Myers was 'still armed when shot.' Family attorneys argue the autopsy evidence contradicts police claims, emphasizing multiple posterior wounds indicate Myers was fleeing. The shooting has sparked renewed protests in St. Louis, drawing comparisons to the 2014 Ferguson incident involving Michael Brown. While both cases involve white officers shooting black teenagers, authorities note Myers was reportedly armed during the encounter. Grand juries are reviewing both cases.

article_content: By Shari Miller | Published: 9 March 2014 | Updated: 10 March 2014 The Globe Theatre faces criticism from human rights groups over plans to stage Hamlet in North Korea, drawing attention to parallels between the play's plot and Kim Jong Un's 2013 execution of his uncle Jang Song Thaek. The production forms part of a two-year global tour visiting 205 nations, beginning on 23 April to coincide with Shakespeare's 450th birth anniversary. Niall Couper of Amnesty International stated: 'North Korea's real-life horrors surpass fictional tragedies. The regime's prison camps subject 100,000 people to torture, rape, starvation, and executions.' The UN has accused North Korea of crimes against humanity and urged accountability through the International Criminal Court. Jang Song Thaek, once Kim Jong Un's mentor and the regime's second-most powerful figure, was executed in December 2013 after being accused of plotting a coup. State media denounced him as 'worse than a dog' and 'human scum.' His extended family members were subsequently purged. Hamlet's themes of familial betrayal and power struggles mirror recent North Korean events. Globe Theatre artistic director Dominic Dromgoole defended the tour, stating the company refuses to boycott nations: 'Everybody means everybody.' The British Embassy has been consulted regarding potential diplomatic sensitivities.

article_content: (CNN) - The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has concluded Kevin Pietersen's international cricket career. A Tuesday announcement confirmed the batsman's exclusion from England's upcoming West Indies tour and ICC World Twenty20 squad in Bangladesh. This decision follows England's 5-0 Ashes series defeat in Australia, with the board stating it's time to 'develop new team dynamics and strategic philosophy.' ECB managing director Paul Downton praised Pietersen as England's record run-scorer (13,797 runs across formats) while stressing organizational priorities: 'While we celebrate Kevin's exceptional career, we must now focus on cultivating team unity for future success.' Pietersen, whose memorable 2005 debut featured two half-centuries against Australia, expressed mixed emotions: 'Representing England brought me immense pride. Though saddened by this conclusion, I remain committed to cricket elsewhere.' Former captain Michael Vaughan questioned the decision on X (formerly Twitter): 'Baffling end for a genius. What made KP unmanageable? @KP24 leaves a void.'

article_content: By Anna Edwards. Published: 13:51 EST, 5 June 2013 | Updated: 13:51 EST, 5 June 2013. A bankrupt businessman shot a solicitor dead, allegedly blaming him for relationship breakdown and home repossession, Salisbury Crown Court heard. Michael Chudley, 63, entered James Ward's office in July 2022 and fatally shot the 58-year-old father of three with a sawn-off shotgun. Mr Ward, managing partner at MGW Law in Devizes, Wiltshire, succumbed to injuries three weeks later. Chudley denies murder charges but admits manslaughter via diminished responsibility - a plea contested by prosecutors. The court heard Chudley threatened receptionist Daphne Courtney to access Ward's office, stating 'I shot him because he made our lives a misery' during arrest. Prosecution alleges premeditation, citing Chudley's written admission of planning the attack while claiming 'autopilot' mental state. Financial disputes stemming from a 2009 building case and subsequent failed lawsuits reportedly motivated Chudley, who faced homelessness after property repossession. Forensic psychiatrist Dr John Sandford testified that Chudley's personality disorder didn't impair rational decision-making, supporting prosecution's murder charge. The trial continues before Mr Justice Bean.

article_content: SARAJEVO, Bosnia-Herzegovina -- Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of Bosnia's Serb-dominated region Republika Srpska, declined to enter a plea Monday regarding charges of defying the international peace envoy overseeing Bosnia's post-war governance. Dodik, a vocal advocate for Serb secession, dismissed the Sarajevo court's legitimacy and openly rejected Bosnia's national authority, reigniting concerns about the country's stability three decades after its devastating 1990s conflict that killed over 100,000 people. The Serb leader claimed procedural irregularities, including the use of Latin script instead of Serbian Cyrillic for legal documents, and refused to stand during the hearing. 'This is political theater, not justice,' Dodik stated following the brief court proceeding. He continues to reject the authority of German diplomat Christian Schmidt, the High Representative for Bosnia appointed in 2021, claiming his position violates international law. Dodik's supporters have staged multiple rallies backing his separatist agenda. Recent threats to arrest Schmidt if he enters Serb-controlled territories and ongoing calls for Republika Srpska's independence directly challenge the U.S.-brokered 1995 Dayton Agreement that ended Bosnia's ethnic war. The agreement established Bosnia's divided structure between Serb, Bosniak, and Croat entities within the nation of 3.2 million people, maintaining an uneasy peace that now faces renewed strain. While facing U.S. and UK sanctions, Dodik maintains Russian support for his separatist policies, reflecting broader geopolitical tensions in the Balkans.

article_content: On June 24 in Natal, Luis Suarez committed the most memorable act of that summer's World Cup by biting Italian defender Giorgio Chiellini. This incident triggered a chain of events that led to the Uruguayan's transfer to Barcelona. Coincidentally, playing that same day was the man who would become Suarez's unexpected replacement at Liverpool. The events of that intense afternoon in northeast Brazil highlight the significant risk Brendan Rodgers is taking by bringing Mario Balotelli back to the Premier League. In the crucial World Cup match against Uruguay that determined Italy's fate, Balotelli delivered a poor performance. After an early foul, he contributed little, received a yellow card for dissent, and was substituted at halftime. Balotelli's World Cup performance reflected his career pattern: a promising start with a goal against England followed by ineffective subsequent games. While Balotelli's off-field behavior might be manageable for Rodgers, questions remain about his development since leaving Manchester City 18 months prior. His £16m transfer raises concerns given his previous Premier League struggles, where he was known for poor training habits and tactical indiscipline. Despite scoring 14 Serie A goals last season, Milan's eagerness to sell remains puzzling. Andrea Pirlo claims Balotelli has matured, but Rodgers faces the challenge of transforming a player who demands constant attention and a fixed striker role. The Liverpool manager's track record with developing talent suggests potential for success, but Balotelli's inflexibility on the pitch makes this a high-stakes gamble for Merseyside.

article_content: In a landmark decision today, the U.S. Supreme Court maintained Michigan's prohibition against considering race in university admissions. The 6-2 ruling affirmed voters' 2006 constitutional amendment granting public institutions authority to exclude racial factors from enrollment decisions. Justice Anthony Kennedy emphasized this case centered on 'who decides admission policies, not the merits of racial preferences.' Dissenting Justice Sonia Sotomayor delivered a forceful 58-page rebuttal, arguing democratic processes without safeguards risk marginalizing minority groups. The majority opinion referenced an earlier 8-7 federal appeals court decision that had challenged the amendment's constitutionality. While Justice Elena Kagan abstained due to prior involvement, five other justices supported the ruling. Data shows decreased African-American enrollment at Michigan and mixed results in California schools - with Latino admissions rising slightly but lagging behind demographic growth - since similar bans took effect. This marks the Court's second affirmative action ruling in recent years, following last June's University of Texas case that tightened race consideration standards. Legal experts suggest these decisions collectively reshape diversity efforts in higher education nationwide.

In dissenso, la giudice Sonia Sotomayor ha presentato un documento di 58 pagine, avvertendo che i processi democratici senza contrappesi possono danneggiare le minoranze. La maggioranza ha richiamato un precedente verdetto 8-7 della corte d'appello. La giudice Elena Kagan non ha partecipato per conflitto d'interessi. I dati rivelano un calo di studenti afroamericani all'Università del Michigan e trend contrastanti in California, con lieve aumento latino non proporzionale alla crescita demografica. Questo è il secondo caso sulle azioni affermative affrontato dalla Corte in due anni, dopo quello del 2022 sull'Università del Texas che ha inasprito le regole sull'uso dei criteri razziali. article_content: The boxing gloves worn by Muhammad Ali during his first Heavyweight Championship victory on February 25, 1964, are being auctioned for $500,000. Then known as Cassius Clay, Ali defeated Sonny Liston in Miami Beach through a seventh-round technical knockout. Liston, then the world's most feared boxer, retired from the match. Trainer Angelo Dundee removed the gloves immediately after the fight, keeping them until his death in 2012. Now showing minor tape-related discoloration, the gloves will be sold by Heritage Auctions on February 25, 2023 - 59 years after the historic match. This coincides with the anniversary of Ali's name change, which he announced one week post-victory following his conversion to Islam. Chris Ivy, Heritage Auctions' sports director, noted: 'These gloves marked Ali's ascent to legendary status. Dundee preserved this crucial piece of boxing history, recognizing its significance. As we approach the 59th anniversary, they stand as testament to Ali's enduring global legacy beyond sports.'

Presentano ora lievi scoloriture dovute ai bendaggi e saranno venduti da Heritage Auctions il 25 febbraio 2023 - a 59 anni dallo storico match. article_content: As Senator Martin Heinrich prepared to celebrate New Mexico's new national monument, scrutiny emerged regarding his past collaboration with environmental activist Dave Foreman. Campaign finance documents show Foreman's wife donated $1,750 to Heinrich's 2012 Senate bid. Earth First! became known for radical environmental actions during the 1990s-2000s, including an abandoned plan to damage power lines serving a nuclear plant. Foreman's original felony charge was reduced to misdemeanor vandalism contingent on five years' probation, culminating in a $250 fine. During Heinrich's chairmanship of the Alliance, several Earth First! affiliates served on its board, with the Foreman home frequently hosting meetings. Historical documentation reveals Foreman's militant environmental philosophy: 'Our goal isn't reform - it's systemic disruption.' This approach sometimes involved publishing personal details of corporate leaders, a tactic that reportedly influenced Unabomber Ted Kaczynski. Investigators noted matching errors in target identification between Kaczynski's manifesto and Earth First! publications. Though Foreman later moderated his approach, policy analysts like Ron Arnold contend his 'rewilding' concept advocates reducing human activity in conservation areas. Requests for comment from opposing political figures and Earth First! representatives went unanswered at publication time.

article_content: Erano passati pochi mesi dal discorso del 3 gennaio 1925 con cui Mussolini annunciò la svolta autoritaria del fascismo quando apparve in libreria un pamphlet edito da Piero Gobetti. Il titolo, *Lo spaccio del bestione trionfante*, seguito dal sottotitolo *Stroncatura di Giovanni Gentile*, segnalava già il tono polemico dell'opera di Adriano Tilgher (1887-1941), già noto come traduttore e filosofo. Nel 1921, Tilgher aveva pubblicato *La crisi mondiale* (saggi del 1918) e *Relativisti contemporanei*, contribuendo al dibattito sulla crisi culturale postbellica. La sua analisi collegava il fascismo al relativismo filosofico, definendolo «assoluto attivismo trapiantato in politica» - formula che Mussolini stesso approvò su *Il Popolo d'Italia* definendola «esattissima». Nato a Resina (oggi Ercolano) da padre renano e madre valdostana, Tilgher sviluppò un pensiero anti-storicista influenzato dal trauma della Grande Guerra. Pur formatosi nell'ambiente crociano, se ne distaccò progressivamente, aderendo nel 1924 all'Unione nazionale antifascista e firmando nel 1925 il Manifesto degli intellettuali antifascisti di Croce. Il pamphlet del 1925, ora ripubblicato da Edizioni di Storia e Letteratura (con postfazione di Gabriele Turi), attacca l'attualismo gentiliano come «filosofia naturale di un'epoca di violenza settaria». La critica a Gentile raggiunge toni personali, definendolo «Calibano intellettuale» e paragonando lo Stato attualista a una «degenerazione bubbonica» dell'hegeliano. Come nota Augusto Del Noce, l'eccesso di polemica personale limitò l'impatto del saggio nonostante l'acume filosofico. Tilgher stesso avrebbe successivamente moderato i toni negli anni seguenti, pur mantenendo una critica radicale allo storicismo.

article_content: La fragilità delle opere d’arte è costituzionale, come quella delle persone. Gli esseri umani sono delicati, patiscono il caldo e il freddo, possono ammalarsi e guarire. Le opere d’arte hanno un vantaggio: non soffrono di malattie mortali. Possono subire alterazioni, ma spesso recuperano il loro stato originario. Come gli organismi viventi, anche materiali come marmo, metalli e pigmenti possono subire processi reversibili. Le opere d’arte non muoiono e hanno una speranza di vita più lunga della nostra. Anche mia madre è fragile, eppure viaggia in auto e in aereo senza problemi. Un’amica centenaria si è lanciata col paracadute. Mario Resca, a sessantadue anni, si sposta continuamente e torna al ministero in salute. Io stesso, pur prezioso, rischio danni viaggiando. Questo vale anche per le opere d’arte: viaggiare in aereo è sconsigliabile ma non impossibile. La polemica sui bronzi di Riace nasce da una metafora di Resca: 'prendono polvere'. In realtà, la polvere protegge. Non è auspicabile lucidarli per esibizioni frequenti, ma trasferimenti occasionali con tecnologie appropriate sono fattibili. I bronzi hanno casse sofisticate che ne permettono persino il galleggiamento. Sono rimasti intatti per 2400 anni sott’acqua: la loro resistenza è provata. Nel 1972, vidi i bronzi una settimana dopo il recupero. Giudicai subito la loro importanza come rari esempi di arte greca del V secolo a.C. Dopo otto anni di restauro, furono esposti a Firenze e al Quirinale. Il sovrintendente Nicosia li spostò senza timori, dimostrando che il restauro fu complesso ma non impossibile. Oggi, dopo 30 anni, la tecnologia può migliorarne ulteriormente la stabilità. Opere più fragili come il Satiro di Mazara o l’Efebo di Mozia hanno viaggiato globalmente. Anche affreschi di Giotto e Botticelli sono stati trasferiti. Non si comprende perché solo i bronzi di Riace siano considerati troppo fragili. La vera fragilità sta nelle menti di chi ne parla: i bronzi potrebbero essere esposti ad Atene, New York e Pechino, promuovendo il patrimonio italiano. Proposte di scambi con l’Auriga di Delfi furono bloccate da pretesti infondati. Le autorità locali di Reggio Calabria ostacolano i prestiti con scuse municipali, ma le opere appartengono allo Stato. Spendere un milione per copie dei bronzi è inutile: solo gli originali attirano il pubblico. Come l’Annunciazione di Leonardo o gli affreschi di Pompei, i bronzi possono viaggiare con precauzioni. Le resistenze ricordano i veti al Cristo morto di Brera o alla Conversione di San Paolo di Caravaggio, opere più fragili dei bronzi. La proposta più assurda viene da Francesco Bonami: sostituire i bronzi con il David di Michelangelo o la Pietà Rondanini, opere intrasportabili. Il David attira 1,3 milioni di turisti all’anno a Firenze: rimuoverlo scatenerebbe proteste. Il vero ostacolo ai prestiti è la mentalità mafiosa, non la fragilità. L’Antimafia dovrebbe gestire l’operazione, a beneficio di Calabria, Italia e mondo.

article_content: Solo per i più accaniti cinefili conta qualcosa il nome di William Randolph Hearst, l’eccentrico editore che per oltre sessant'anni (dal 1887 al 1951) guidò il più grande impero giornalistico statunitense. La sua figura viene spesso associata allo scontro con Orson Welles, che nel 1940 ritrasse il 'tiranno' mediatico nel capolavoro *Quarto potere* (noto in inglese come *Citizen Kane*). Hearst, quasi governatore di New York grazie al sostegno popolare, fu anche artefice di campagne sensazionaliste come il caso Evangelina Cisneros, strumentalizzato per creare tensioni tra USA e Cuba. Il castello di San Simeon, costruito tra il 1919 e il 1947 su progetto dell'architetta Julia Morgan, rappresenta il culmine della sua ambizione. Con torri ispirate alla cattedrale di Ronda e la Piscina di Nettuno decorata con reperti di Villa Aldobrandini, la residenza ospitò star come Charlie Chaplin e Clark Gable. La compagna Marion Davies, immortalata come 'nuova Afrodite' attraverso sculture a sua somiglianza, dominò per trent'anni questa reggia dove Hearst accumulò opere d'arte sfruttando agevolazioni doganali.

I 209 miliardi stanziati dall'UE dovranno affrontare sfide cruciali: dalla transizione ecologica all'innovazione tecnologica. Tra le priorità emerge il nesso tra qualità dell'aria e salute pubblica, evidenziato durante la pandemia. Studi internazionali rivelano che l'esposizione cronica all'inquinamento aumenta la vulnerabilità alle infezioni respiratorie. La ricerca sulla SARS dimostra un +84% di mortalità nelle aree ad alto tasso di smog. Mentre persiste il dibattito sul possibile ruolo di trasporto virale da parte del particolato, è accertato che l'inquinamento compromette la salute respiratoria. Con 400mila decessi annui in Europa legati allo smog (60mila in Italia), il piano di ripresa offre un'opportunità storica per rivoluzionare mobilità sostenibile ed efficienza energetica, settori cruciali per la riduzione dell'impatto ambientale.
